1	# Measurement
2	
3	Two things, both small: a weekly record of how Caliper compares with react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on five public repos, and `just bench` for a change that touches the resolver. Nothing here blocks a pull request.
4	
5	## Weekly record
6	
7	`.github/workflows/weekly.yml` runs on Mondays and by hand. `scripts/corpora.py` fetches each repo at a pinned commit and installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile (lifecycle scripts off, caches under `.corpora/`, gitignored), then removes tests, stories, demos and `.d.ts` files from the source directory so every tool reads the same files. `scripts/weekly.py` runs the tools.
8	
9	| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
12	| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
13	| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
14	| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
15	| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |
16	
17	It records, per corpus and tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start and Node start included), and the size of Caliper's canonical JSON. Caliper runs with `--load-dependencies`; its time is the median of five runs. RDT and react-docgen run once each.
18	
19	Each run's peak RSS is that process's own. `scripts/corpora.py` starts every measured command through a small helper that forks it and reads its `wait4` usage. Reading it straight from the weekly script gave one number for every run after the largest: on Linux a child's `ru_maxrss` starts at the highest RSS its parent ever had, and the script's own peak (it holds RDT's output for a large corpus) became every later tool's "peak". The first weekly record shows 1,593 MiB for all three tools on shadcn, antd and spectrum, which is that. `scripts/test_weekly.py` checks that a large parent no longer leaks in.
20	
21	### The reference
22	
23	Recall is measured against RDT's output, cleaned in two steps. Both are by what RDT reports, never by library or name lists, and `weekly.json` keeps their counts (`reference` per corpus) so a change in either is visible.
24	
25	| Step | Rule |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Not components, left out | More than half of the props are declared in TypeScript's own `lib.*.d.ts` (the parameter is a `string`, a `Request`, a function: `GET`, `loadHighlighter`, `convertLegacyProps`). The name is a hook's (`use` and a capital). The only props are a `value` (and `children`) declared by `@types/react`, which is a context's Provider (`FormContext`). The name starts lowercase, is not the file's or directory's name (RDT names a default export after those) and no prop comes from `@types/react`, so it is no JSX tag and takes no tag's attributes (`genLinkStyle`, `generateMetadata`). Every prop is a `Promise<...>`, which a router hands over (`page`). |
28	| Repeats, counted once | RDT lists one component under each file that re-exports it, and names a default export after the file or directory (antd's `col/index.tsx` default-exports `Col` from `../grid` and RDT reports `col` there; Caliper reports the defining file). An entry that Caliper does not report in its own file pairs by evidence: where the default export, or the named export, of RDT's file is defined (followed through `export default X`, `import`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }`), or else the file that declares its props when Caliper reports a component of that name there. The same evidence works inside one file: a default export that is another name (`const InternalButton = ...; export default InternalButton`, which RDT calls `button`), or the component whose `displayName` RDT reports. Both are guarded: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own, so a member such as `Form.List` is never paired with `Form`, and a Caliper key that another RDT entry matches exactly is never a target. A call around the name (`memo(Foo)`, `React.forwardRef(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, { Item })`), a type assertion (`Foo as T`, `Foo satisfies T`, `Foo!`) and a chain of local aliases (`const A = memo(B)`) lead to the declaration; Caliper's `displayName` for it counts as its name. Entries that pair with the same Caliper component are one reference item. |
29	
30	The record shows, per corpus: RDT's entries with props, how many are not components, how many repeats were merged, the reference size, how many match in the same file, how many are paired (by default export, default alias, `displayName`, named export or declaration) and how many stay unpaired. `weekly.json` also records the `reference_version`: the rules above are version 2 (a record without it is version 1), and recall is not compared with a record made under other rules, so a change to them cannot read as a regression or hide one. Pairing needs the names to agree: the component the export resolves to must have the name Caliper reports, so an entry never pairs with an unrelated component just because it is the only one in its file. When several RDT entries pair to one component, the reference takes the props of the entry in the component's own file, else the union of the repeats'. An unpaired item is a component Caliper does not report where RDT does, and it stays in the denominator.
31	
32	The 2026-10-31 effect on the pinned corpora, Caliper's component recall (own and `@types/react` props are unchanged by the exclusions and move only a little with the pairing):
33	
34	| Corpus | Reference before |                                           After | Components before | After |
35	| ------ | ---------------: | ----------------------------------------------: | ----------------: | ----: |
36	| shadcn |             1594 |                   1573 (21 left out, 0 repeats) |             95.2% | 96.5% |
37	| antd   |              258 | 203 (43 left out, 12 repeats merged, 12 paired) |             64.0% | 81.3% |
38	
39	Exclusions alone give 76.7% on antd, pairing alone 68.3%.
40	
41	The 2026-11-02 pairing (same-file default aliases, `displayName`, wrappers, assertions, alias chains), replayed on the pinned commits with RDT's output and Caliper's at that day's `main`:
42	
43	| Corpus | Reference before | After | Components before |        After |
44	| ------ | ---------------: | ----: | ----------------: | -----------: |
45	| shadcn |             1573 |  1573 |      1518 (96.5%) | 1518 (96.5%) |
46	| antd   |              207 |   202 |       165 (79.7%) |  186 (92.1%) |
47	
48	Each corpus entry's `reference.unmatched` says why the items Caliper reports nowhere are missing: `by_cause` counts them and `listed` names the first 15 of each cause as `file: name`. The cause is what the item's file shows, so it says where to look, not what is wrong:
49	
50	| Cause | The file shows |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| `compound_member` | An assignment to a member of another component (`Form.List = List`). |
53	| `object_member` | The name as a function-valued key of an object literal (`logo: () => ...`). |
54	| `dependency` | An alias of something a package exports (`const Tooltip = Recharts.Tooltip`), or an export that ends in a package. |
55	| `call_result` | A value a call builds (`createIcon(...)`, `generateCalendar(...)`). |
56	| `file_with_other_components`, `file_without_components` | A declaration Caliper does not report, in a file where it reports others, or none. |
57	
58	The 14 antd items still unpaired in the weekly run of 2026-11-06 (16 when this was first written) are not pairing cases: the date picker and calendar families (built by factory functions), `Parent.Member` entries Caliper reports under the parent (`Form.List`, `Mentions.Option`, `TreeSelect.TreeNode`), and helpers RDT lists as components (`confirm`, `dropIndicator`). shadcn has no re-export of this kind in the pinned commit, so nothing pairs there; its unpaired items are `Icons.logo`-style object members, aliases such as `const ComboboxRoot = Primitive.Root` and factory results, which Caliper does not detect.
59	
60	Recall is measured against that reference, on the components both tools report (same file, same name, or paired):
61	
62	| Measure              | Meaning                                                                                   |
63	| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| Components           | The reference's components that the tool also reports                                     |
65	| Own props            | Of those components, RDT's props not declared by `@types/react` that the tool lists       |
66	| `@types/react` props | RDT's props that `@types/react` declares (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `ref`) that the tool lists |
67	| ... with layers      | The same two, also counting a prop held in a collapsed inheritance layer                  |
68	
69	By default (`collapseInheritedProps: dependencies`) Caliper collapses a large ambient inherited dependency source (DOM and ARIA attributes, style systems; more than 30 props) into a layer (ADR 0012; `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md`, Collapse) and lists only its notable members as props. A dependency's own API is listed in full (a source past 200 props that is not ambient by name still collapses). The Storybook addon runs with `collapseInheritedProps: none`, which lists every inherited prop; the layers below are what the CLI, the NAPI binding and agents reading the output see. A prop in a layer is in the output, named by the layer's `members`, but is not in the flat list, so the table reports both: the plain columns say what the default output lists, "with layers" says what it holds. react-docgen writes no layers, so its two columns are equal.
70	
71	react-docgen parses each file with its default resolver and importer, as Storybook does. The importer follows relative and package imports to the file that declares a type, so a props interface imported from a sibling file is read. It does no type inference: it lists none of React's inherited attributes, and a generic, mapped or conditional type stays the source text. That is the point of the comparison. A file it throws on is counted (`failed`) and listed (`failedFiles`), not dropped silently.
72	
73	The run uploads `weekly.json` and a table to the job summary, which opens with a short "how to read these numbers" paragraph and the headline (below). It compares with the last successful run's `weekly.json` and opens, or comments on, one issue labelled `weekly-measurement` only for what is a problem on its own (see "The headline"): a wrong type above the gate or higher than last week, a silent-wrong answer to a reader's question, or a whole run over a budget. Drift in time, memory, recall against RDT and the agent correct rate is listed in the summary under "Changes since last week" and opens nothing: a shared CI machine moves by 10% or more on its own, and recall against RDT is how much of RDT's output we also report, not whether our types are right. There is no committed baseline: the previous run is the baseline for what rose.
74	
75	### TypeScript's checker as the oracle
76	
77	RDT has mistakes of its own. With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript-beta/sync`, the `7.1.0-beta` package) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`, extracted with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported --load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`. The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts, for Caliper, RDT and react-docgen, and the headline below. `agree` is the loose number; `wrong` is the one that matters and the one the weekly issue gates on, but the comparator has artifacts that make it both over- and under-report. `docs/rdt-differences.md` lists every class of disagreement with an example, how it is counted and whether the comparator scored it right. The checker is a beta and the backend that uses it is an opt-in (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`), so a disagreement is a reason to look, not a verdict on its own.
78	
79	| Verdict | Meaning |
80	| --- | --- |
81	| Identical | Both sides describe the same type |
82	| Spelled | The same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it |
83	| Less precise | Caliper's type is looser or left unevaluated |
84	| Wrong | Caliper's type describes something else (an omitted key that came back, an object with no fields for a callable) |
85	| Checker any/error | The checker has no type |
86	
87	#### All three tools against the checker
88	
89	RDT and react-docgen are held to the checker too, by the same rules, so the comparison does not take either as the truth. `oracle.ts` also takes the dumps `scripts/rdt.mjs` and `scripts/rdg.mjs` write (`--rdt`, `--rdg`). Both tools state a type as source text, which `apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts` reads with TypeScript's parser into the shape the comparison uses; a type a tool printed in part (`Foo<...>`, `{string}`) or did not evaluate is unreadable, which scores as less precise and never as wrong. The scoring is `apps/oracle/src/tool-score.ts`.
90	
91	The **universe** is every own prop the checker finds on an exported function whose only parameter, or `props` parameter, is the props type. React's inherited DOM attributes, `ref` and `key` are not in it. It includes some functions that are not components, because the checker has no notion of one, so read the shares as a comparison between tools, not as a share of real components. For each tool the record has, in `oracle.tools`:
92	
93	- **Agreement of the whole universe** (`agree_universe`): identical or spelled, over every prop in the universe. A prop the tool omits counts against it. This is the comparison between tools; Caliper's own headline is below.
94	- **Agreement of listed props** (`agree_listed`) and the share the checker contradicts (`wrong_listed`): over the props the tool lists, which is what Caliper's own `agree` and `wrong` have always been.
95	- **Omitted props**, by where the checker declares them (`missing_by_stratum`): the component's own file, another file of the corpus, or a dependency. A prop Caliper lists only as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer is counted apart (`collapsed`), because that is a choice and not an omission.
96	- **Why a prop is omitted** (`missing_by_reason`): the tool reports no such component, it reports the component but not the prop, or it threw on the file.
97	- **react-docgen's thrown files** (`failed_files`): files its default resolver throws on, 17% to 21% of the files on antd and shadcn. Their props are omitted, so they cost react-docgen agreement; they have their own column so the cost is visible.
98	
99	`oracle.shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` keep their meaning, so the weekly history does not move. A local run on antd and shadcn at the commit that added this, with the default collapse (the weekly record collapses nothing, and reads 44.7% and 90.4% for Caliper), reads, for the whole universe: Caliper 39.7% and 40.1% (its `collapsed` layers and any component it does not report count against it), RDT 44.8% and 84.8%, react-docgen 24.6% and 1.9%. This comparison between tools is information, never a gate, and the rules were validated on antd and shadcn; the weekly run produces all five corpora.

101	### The headline
102	
103	What matters is whether the types Storybook and agents are shown are right, not whether Caliper matches RDT. The headline (`scripts/headline.py`, read from `oracle.tools.caliper_reported`, which `apps/oracle/src/tool-score.ts` `scoreReported` computes) takes every own prop the checker finds on a component Caliper reports, so a function the checker takes for a component and Caliper rightly ignores does not count against it, and sorts each prop into one kind:
104	
105	- **Correct**: the same type as the checker, or the same type spelled differently.
106	- **Less precise**: vaguer than the checker's (a name left unexpanded, `string` for a union of literals), not contradicting it.
107	- **Wrong**: describes something else. This is the gate.
108	- **No checker type**: the checker has none either (an unresolved import, `any`).
109	- **Missing**: Caliper reports the component but not the prop.
110	- **Named only**: Caliper lists the prop by name as a member of a collapsed inheritance layer, so it is surfaced but a reader sees no type for it. It is counted apart, as neither correct nor wrong, because correct values reached through a layer are a win and a bare name is not.
111	
112	The record keeps the counts per corpus as `headline`, next to the unchanged `oracle` and `recall` fields. The shares in the summary are of every prop of the components Caliper reports. The gate uses the wrong share of the props whose type can be judged (correct, less precise and wrong), so a corpus with many layer-only props does not dilute it.
113	
114	The issue opens when, on any corpus:
115	
116	- more than 0.1% of the judged props are wrong, or the wrong share is higher than last week's (the count is not trustworthy in either direction yet: the comparator reads an index signature as a property and so reports wrong props that are right, and it scores a dropped `Partial` or `Omit` as less precise or identical, so wrong answers never reach it; `docs/rdt-differences.md`);
117	- a question a reader is asked is answered silent-wrong (`scripts/agent_eval.py`);
118	- a whole run is over a budget: 2 s or 600 MiB with dependencies loaded, the default (`BUDGETS` in `scripts/headline.py`). The budgets are user-facing limits, not week-over-week ones; Chakra, the largest corpus, ran in 0.24 s and 378 MiB in the weekly run of 2026-11-06.
119	
120	Recall against RDT stays information. A local run on antd and shadcn at the commit that added this, with the default collapse, reads: antd 83.7% correct, 6.0% less precise, 0.00% wrong, 10.2% named only (3,426 props); shadcn 54.4% correct, 5.1% less precise, 0.06% wrong (0.096% of the judged props, just under the gate), 0.4% missing, 39.6% named only (13,918 props). The weekly record collapses nothing (`--collapse-inherited-props none`), so named only is 0 there; its run of 2026-11-06 reads antd 94.0% correct, 6.0% less precise, 0 wrong, and shadcn 93.8% correct, 5.3% less precise, 8 wrong (0.058% of the shared props), 0.4% missing (`headline` in `weekly.json`, `main` at `c5fbb33e`). Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum read in that run: 90.9%, 100.0% and 83.7% agree, with 0, 1 and 22 wrong. Of Spectrum's 22, the comparator's index-signature artifact accounts for all (`docs/rdt-differences.md`), so that gate firing is false until the comparator is corrected.

122	### An independent reference
123	
124	The oracle above scores a tool against the TypeScript checker alone. That cannot judge a mode that uses the checker, which would agree with itself, and it cannot say which side is right when they differ. `scripts/reference_sample.py` (`apps/oracle/src/reference.ts`) judges a sample of props by two methods that fail differently:
125	
126	- **A, the checker's type.** The same normalized type the oracle compares (`oracle-checker.ts`).
127	- **B, the declared type.** What the prop's declaration writes, read from source text with TypeScript's parser (`reference-declared.ts`), never from the checker's type printer. The checker is asked only where the declaration is. B abstains where the declaration leaves the type to be computed (an indexed access, `keyof`, a conditional type), writes no type (an unannotated member, a method with no return type, or a value such as `count: 1` in an object literal that the checker infers the type of), has no declaration (a mapped type's synthesized member), or has several that differ.
128	
129	They are compared with the oracle's own rules (`oracle-compare.ts`), B standing in for the tool. Identical or spelled is agreement. B looser than A (a name or a type parameter A evaluated) is B saying less, so A stands alone. B contradicting A is **contested**: it is listed in the review file for a person, never counted for or against a tool. Where A has no type (`any`, an error) and B does, B stands alone.
130	
131	A tool's prop is then **correct** (agrees with the reference), **less precise**, **wrong**, **contested**, **no reference**, **missing**, or **layer**. A component lists a prop when it is in its `props` or its `notableInherited` (the curated props of a collapsed source, which a props table lists after the component's own; the component's own wins a clash). Where the declaration stands alone and only names a type (the checker could not resolve it), a tool that gives the same name is correct, and one that gives another type is at most less precise, because the name cannot be seen into. A prop the tool does not list but a collapsed inheritance layer names (`inheritance[].members`, an interned name list in the canonical JSON) is a `layer`: surfaced, but with no type to judge, so it is neither credited as correct nor counted as missing. Each verdict keeps which methods stood behind it (`both`, `checker`, `declaration`), so a count of correct props says how many were corroborated by B and how many rest on A alone.
132	
133	The sample is every prop a `--list` file names (`[{ corpus, file, component, prop }]`, for example the props two modes differ on) plus a seeded control sample, 100 per corpus by default, stratified so it is not all `string` and `boolean`. A prop falls in the first of these it fits: listed, generic, mapped (`Pick`, `Omit`, `Partial`, …), intersection, function, union of literals, from a dependency, an `@types/react` attribute (at most three per component), from another project file, own. With a tool's output given, the control sample is drawn from the components the tool reports, because the checker takes any exported one-parameter function for a component; pass `allComponents` in the config to draw from all. The candidates are capped at `universeCap` (8,000 by default), taken from the corpus's files in a seeded order, so a corpus larger than that is sampled from part of it; the number collected is printed. A listed prop the checker cannot find (a wrong component name, a file not in the list, a prop it does not see) is judged nowhere, so the report names it (`listed.missing`) beside how many were requested and found, and counts the entries that name a corpus the run does not have (`listed_for_other_corpora`).
134	
135	```bash
136	scripts/reference_sample.py --bin target/release/caliper-docgen --corpus antd --corpus shadcn [--per-corpus 300] [--list diff.json]
137	```
138	
139	The report (`reference.json`) counts, per corpus, how the reference was reached (`agreed_both`, `checker_only`, `declaration_only`, `contested`, `none`), why B abstained, and the tool's outcomes in total, by stratum and by origin. `review.md` lists the contested props with both types and the declaration's path; `reference.json.rows.json` has every judged prop. Output goes to `--out-dir`, a temporary directory by default.
140	
141	What it does not establish:
142	
143	- A and B read the same declaration. They corroborate each other where B can read a type, and say nothing where it cannot (a computed type, which is where a checker-backed mode matters most). Count `checker_only` as props with no independent evidence; a labelled sample is the independent check for those.
144	- `oracle-compare.ts` reads a widened primitive of another kind as `less precise`, not `wrong` (`number` against `'a' | 'b'`). Changing that would move every historical oracle number, so the reference inherits it.
145	- The sample is the components Caliper reports, so it says nothing about components Caliper misses.

147	### Layer-only props
148	
149	**Which configuration this describes.** The CLI, the NAPI binding and the Vite plugin collapse by default (`collapseInheritedProps: 'dependencies'`). The Storybook addon does not: it defaults to `'none'` (`packages/storybook/src/provider.ts`), which lists every inherited prop with its type, so in a Storybook props table no prop is layer-only. What follows describes what a default CLI, NAPI or agent consumer gets; the addon's configuration is the fully expanded run, reported beside it.
150	
151	A collapsed inheritance layer (a dependency source declaring more than 30 props, `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md`, "Collapse") reaches a reader as a list of names, `inheritance[].members`, with no types. `scripts/layer_only_props.py` (`apps/oracle/src/layer-only.ts`) takes every such prop that the component's `props` and `notableInherited` do not list, over all components of a corpus, and sorts it into two classes by a rule that reads only the layer's file, the layer's type name and the prop's name. The first clause that fits decides:
152	
153	1. **dom file** → ambient. The layer is declared in `@types/react`, or in react-aria's `@react-types/shared/src/dom.d.ts`.
154	2. **dom type** → ambient. The layer's type is `GlobalDOMEvents`, `DOMAttributes`, `AriaAttributes`, `AllHTMLAttributes`, `SVGAttributes`, `*HTMLAttributes` or `Aria*Attributes`.
155	3. **style type** → ambient. The layer's type is `*StyleProps`, `SystemProps`, or `Space|Layout|Color|Typography|Border|Flex|Grid|Position|Shadow|Background` followed by `Props`.
156	4. **global attribute** → ambient. The prop is one every element has (`GLOBAL_ATTRIBUTES` in `layer-only.ts`: `className`, `style`, `id`, `title`, `lang`, `dir`, `hidden`, `tabIndex`, `role`, `slot`, …), or starts `aria-` or `data-`. `value`, `defaultValue`, `type`, `name` and `disabled` are not in it: they are element-specific, and a dependency's component often uses them as its own API.
157	5. **dependency api** → API. Anything else a collapsed layer names: the modes, state and composition props of a dependency's component.
158	
159	The 20 API props that matter most are chosen by category first (state, then mode, composition, constraint, data, other, by the prop's name), then by the number of components it is layer-only in. The report gives each its declaring layer, its declared type (read from the layer's `.d.ts`), and why it matters.
160	
161	```bash
162	scripts/layer_only_props.py --bin target/release/caliper-docgen --corpus antd --corpus shadcn [--runs 3]
163	```
164	
165	Measured on antd and shadcn (Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum are not run). These figures predate the last change to the count: an `Omit` now drops the omitted props from a collapsed layer's `members` (`resolver/alias.rs`), and `expandedDependencySources` skips collapsed sources that list a curated `className`. The layer-only, API and "listed in full" rows, and the "ambient by clause 1 to 3" figure of 13 the proposal below relies on, have not been re-measured since; re-run `scripts/layer_only_props.py` before quoting them.

168	| --------------------------------------------------- | --------: | ----------: |
169	| Layer-only props (component × prop)                 |       669 |       6,774 |
170	| API / ambient                                       |   664 / 5 | 267 / 6,507 |
171	| Distinct (layer, prop), API / ambient               |   320 / 3 |     89 / 69 |
172	| Components with at least one API layer-only prop    | 22 of 253 |  6 of 1,901 |
173	| Collapsed layers (all above 30)                     |        10 |           3 |
174	| … of which 31 to 40 props / 41 to 60 / 61 and over  | 5 / 4 / 1 |   1 / 0 / 2 |

177	| Dependency sources listed in full (all 30 or fewer) |        46 |         314 |

180	shadcn's ambient mass is one layer: react-aria's `GlobalDOMEvents`, 64 handlers on 106 components. Its API props are react-day-picker's `PropsBase` (75 props) and Base UI's `ComboboxRootProps` (38). In antd, nearly everything collapsed is a dependency's API: `@rc-component`'s `IDialogPropTypes`, `BaseSelectProps`, `InputNumberProps`, `MenuProps` and the like, so with the default collapse a CLI, NAPI or agent consumer gets `visible`, `onClose`, `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange` as names, with no type. The addon's `none` lists them with their types.
181	
182	What this says about the size rule: it is right where a source happens to be both large and ambient, and wrong where it is large and API. A source of 31 props is collapsed and one of 30 is listed, whatever is in it; 36% and 30% of the API props sit in the 31 to 40 band. It also lists small ambient sources in full (13 in shadcn).
183	
184	**Proposal: collapse by relevance, not size.** Collapse a dependency source when it is ambient by clause 1 to 3, decided from the source's name and file before anything in it is resolved, whatever its size. Do not collapse a source for being large: list its members, keeping clause 4's global attributes as a name list. This changes the resolver (`collapse_inherited_props`), which this measurement does not.

186	Who it is for: the default CLI, NAPI and agent consumers, which collapse by size today and so hold the API props above as names. The Storybook addon already lists everything (`none`) and would see no change in its API props; it could adopt the rule to stop listing ambient names, which the "expanding every layer" row prices in output size but which was not measured as a session's payload.

211	## Checker modes
212	
213	`scripts/checker_modes.py` measures the experimental TypeScript 7.1 checker modes against the structural default on the corpora `scripts/corpora.py` sets up. It is run by hand for now and is not part of the weekly record.
214	
215	```bash
216	cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen && pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
217	python3 scripts/checker_modes.py --bin target/release/caliper-docgen --runs 3 --count 50 --fallbacks \
218	  --out report.json --diff-out diff.json --pairs-out pairs.json
219	```
220	
221	What it runs, per corpus: the structural default (`extract --format rdt`), the same with `--experimental-semantic-types` (the CLI's whole-project checker pass), and one lazy session driven the way the Storybook addon drives it (`scripts/checker_modes_session.mjs`: `createSession`, `initializeSessionIndex`, then `sessionComponentAnswers` per component) with the checker off and with `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` at a 150 ms and a 600 ms wait. `--fallbacks` also runs the CLI and a session against a missing `tsc` and one that exits at once.
222	
223	The settings are the Storybook addon's (`createDocgenProvider` in `packages/storybook/src/provider.ts`): dependency types loaded, `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`, a lazy session, and the NAPI defaults for the rest (`htmlAttributes: 'full'`, the on-disk cache on). The CLI runs pass the same props settings (`--load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none --html-attributes full`) so that the structural and the checker run list the same props. A test reads the addon's source and fails if those defaults change. What the sessions leave out is the per-story look at the files (`ensureFresh`, a few milliseconds on a large project) and `warmUp`/`fillAfter`, both off in the addon by default.
224	
225	What it reports:
226	
227	- Wall time and peak RSS, median with min and max over `--runs` runs, and the machine's load average before and after. Peak RSS is the largest single process (`corpora.run_once`), so a CLI checker run reports the larger of Caliper and `tsc`. A session reports whole-process figures only with the checker off: an on-demand run sleeps before asking the same components a second time, so the time and memory of that script mean nothing next to the checker-off run, and its own step timings are reported instead. The checker's size comes from polling `ps` from the parent while the session runs, never from inside the session, because a measurement between two requests would give a slow checker idle time that the timings do not count. The checker is the direct child of that run's session driver that is a `tsc` in `--api` mode. It is found by what it is, not by a string in a command line: the driver's and the measuring helper's own command lines carry the `tsc` path in their JSON options, and either can use more memory than the checker. The path is not compared either, because the configured `bin/tsc` is a launcher and what runs is the platform binary it resolves to (`@typescript/typescript-<platform>/lib/tsc --api --async --cwd <dir>`). When no such process is seen (a missing `tsc`, or `ps` gave no listing) the size is `None` and prints as n/a, never 0.
228	- First load for a session, one request at a time in a seeded order that is the same in every mode: start (create plus index), the first component, and the first 10 and 50 components asked. A figure for more components than were asked is `None`, not the last one reached. The first of the `--runs` runs starts with an empty cache directory (cold), the others with the cache it left (warm), and both are reported.
229	- For the on-demand mode: the share of first requests the checker answered within the wait, how many timed out, how many kept the structural result for the checker's own reasons (not exported, a class component, generic props), and the share answered once the late answers had arrived.
230	- The props that differ from the structural result: type, required, default and presence. `@types/react` props are counted apart (the whole-project checker pass leaves them out), and a type that differs only in spelling (spacing, `| undefined`, union order, `Array<T>`) is counted as cosmetic. A rest or optional parameter marker is a difference. Each remaining difference gets a coarse category: `only_checker`, `only_structural`, `parameter_marker_lost`, `checker_longer` or `checker_shorter` (the checker's text is more than 20 characters and more than 1.5 times longer or shorter, a length test that says nothing about why, so a longer text may be an alias written out, an object type or a function type), and `other_type`. `--diff-out` has one row per differing prop (without `@types/react` and cosmetic rows, unless `--diff-all`), `--pairs-out` one entry per distinct pair of structural and checker facts with a count, a category and an example, most common first.
231	- The checker oracle's verdict on each mode, for information only: the shares of shared props it calls identical or spelled differently (agree), less precise, and wrong. The oracle is the same checker, so it agrees with a checker mode almost by construction, and it credits the structural result for keeping a type's alias name while it scores the checker's expanded union as less precise (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). Do not read that agree figure as accuracy; judging the checker modes needs a reference that is not the checker. The oracle step runs the CLI with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported --load-dependencies` and the default collapse; the weekly record's own oracle step collapses nothing (`--collapse-inherited-props none`).

252	## What this replaces
253	
254	Before the weekly record, four workflows (Equivalence, Parity, Scorecard and Allow-list empty) ran against every pull request or `main` push, backed by `scripts/equivalence.py`, a per-pull-request allow-list directory and two committed baselines. They caught one regression in speed and one in output that review would have missed. They also failed on runner noise, on bases that had moved and on their own allow-list, and a lot of one week of merge work went to keeping them green. Git history has them.

84	def rss_mib(ru_maxrss, platform=sys.platform):
85	    """`ru_maxrss` in MiB: bytes on macOS, kilobytes on Linux."""
86	    return ru_maxrss / (2**20 if platform == 'darwin' else 1024)

89	def measure_child(args):
90	    """Fork and exec `args`, wait for it, and return (wall seconds, peak RSS MiB, exit code) of that one process. Meant
91	    to run in a small, fresh process (`run_once`): on Linux a child's `ru_maxrss` starts from the largest RSS its parent
92	    ever had (the kernel carries the parent's high-water mark across exec), so a parent that once held a large result
93	    reports that number for every child after it. `os.fork` rather than `vfork` keeps the mark at this process's size."""
94	    start = time.perf_counter()
95	    pid = os.fork()
96	    if pid == 0:
97	        try:
98	            os.execvp(args[0], args)
99	        except OSError as error:
100	            os.write(2, f'cannot run {args[0]}: {error}\n'.encode())
101	        finally:
102	            os._exit(127)
103	    _, status, usage = os.wait4(pid, 0)
104	    return time.perf_counter() - start, rss_mib(usage.ru_maxrss), os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)

107	def run_once(args, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL):
108	    """Wall seconds and peak RSS in MiB of one process, measured by a small helper process so that this process's own
109	    memory never leaks into the number. A helper that fails, a result it did not write and a command that cannot run or
110	    exits non-zero are each a RuntimeError saying what happened, with the end of the helper's stderr."""
111	    command = ' '.join(args)
112	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('r', suffix='.json') as result:
113	        helper = [sys.executable, '-I', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'measure', result.name, '--'] + list(args)
114	        done = subprocess.run(helper, stdout=stdout, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, errors='replace')
115	        detail = done.stderr.strip()[-500:]
116	        if done.returncode != 0:
117	            raise RuntimeError(f'the measuring helper failed (exit {done.returncode}) running {command}: {detail}')
118	        try:
119	            seconds, rss, code = json.load(result)
120	        except ValueError as error:
121	            raise RuntimeError(f'the measuring helper wrote no result for {command}: {error}') from error
122	    if code != 0:
123	        raise RuntimeError(f'{command} exited with {code}' + (f': {detail}' if detail else ''))
124	    return seconds, rss

172	def fetch(corpus, checkout, sparse):
173	    shutil.rmtree(checkout, ignore_errors=True)
174	    os.makedirs(checkout)
175	    git('init', '-q', cwd=checkout)
176	    git('remote', 'add', 'origin', f"https://github.com/{corpus['repo']}.git", cwd=checkout)
177	    flags = []
178	    if sparse:

180	        flags = ['--filter=blob:none']
181	    # Network steps retry: one dropped connection shouldn't fail a scheduled run.
182	    for attempt in range(3):
183	        try:
184	            git('fetch', '-q', '--depth', '1', *flags, 'origin', corpus['commit'], cwd=checkout)
185	            git('checkout', '-q', 'FETCH_HEAD', cwd=checkout)
186	            return
187	        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:

266	        ensure_package_managers(base, env, log)
267	    # The corpora's own package managers can need an older Node than this repository's (Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and
268	    # React Spectrum pin, crashes under Node 26). Only their installs run under it.
269	    if args.install_node_dir:
270	        env['PATH'] = os.path.abspath(args.install_node_dir) + os.pathsep + env['PATH']
271	    failed = []
272	    for corpus in selected(args.corpus):
273	        if ready(corpus, corpora_dir, sparse=False):
274	            print(f"{corpus['name']}: ready at {corpus['commit'][:12]}")
275	            continue
276	        checkout = os.path.join(corpora_dir, corpus['clone'])
277	        log_path = os.path.join(base, 'logs', f"install-{corpus['name']}.log")
278	        try:
279	            print(f"{corpus['name']}: fetching and installing with {corpus['manager']}", flush=True)
280	            fetch(corpus, checkout, sparse=False)
281	            with open(log_path, 'w') as log:
282	                install(corpus, checkout, base, env, log)
283	            prune(os.path.join(checkout, corpus['src']))
284	            with open(os.path.join(checkout, MARKER), 'w') as f:
285	                f.write(corpus['commit'] + ':installed')
286	        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
287	            # One corpus failing must not hide the others: say which one and why, then carry on with the rest.
288	            failed.append(corpus['name'])
289	            print(f"{corpus['name']}: setup FAILED ({error})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
290	    if failed:
291	        sys.exit(f"setup failed for: {', '.join(failed)}; see the install logs in {os.path.join(base, 'logs')}")

294	def main():
295	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
296	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
297	    p = sub.add_parser('setup', help='fetch, install and prune the corpora')
298	    p.add_argument('--corpora', default=DEFAULT_DIR)
299	    p.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[])
300	    p.add_argument('--sparse', action='store_true', help='fetch the source directory only; install nothing')
301	    p.add_argument('--install-node-dir', help="a directory with the `node` the corpora's installs should use")

306	    if args.command == 'measure':

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The weekly record: Caliper, react-docgen-typescript (RDT) and react-docgen on the five pinned corpora.
3	
4	For each corpus it records, per tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start included), and for
5	Caliper the canonical JSON's size. Recall is measured against RDT: of the components RDT reports with props, how many
6	the tool also reports (same file, same name), and of their props, how many it lists, split into the props `@types/react`
7	declares and the rest. react-docgen follows imports to the file that declares a type but infers nothing, and lists none
8	of React's props. With --oracle it also records how often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts each tool's prop types,
9	over every prop the checker finds, and the headline of scripts/headline.py: how many of the props of the components Caliper
10	reports are right. With --agent-eval it also asks a fixed list of questions about real components and scores what a
11	reader of Caliper's output answers against the checker (scripts/agent_eval.py).
12	
13	--previous FILE compares with an earlier record (the last green run's artifact) and writes --issue FILE for the workflow
14	to open or update one issue with, when a wrong type is above the gate or rises, a reader's question is answered
15	silent-wrong, or a whole run is over a budget (scripts/headline.py). Drift in time, memory and recall against RDT is
16	listed in the summary, not alarmed on. Nothing here fails a pull request.
17	
18	Usage: scripts/weekly.py --bin BIN [--corpus NAME]... [--corpora DIR] [--work DIR] [--runs N] [--oracle] [--agent-eval]
19	                         [--previous FILE] [--baseline-failed] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--issue FILE]

120	LIB_FILE = re.compile(r'/typescript/lib/lib\.[^/]*\.d\.ts$')
121	REACT_DIR = 'node_modules/@types/react/'
122	EXTENSIONS = ('', '.tsx', '.ts', '/index.tsx', '/index.ts')
123	# An identifier inside any number of calls (`memo(forwardRef(Foo))`, `React.memo(Foo)`, `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`),
124	# followed by what ends an argument or an expression: `, ) ; !`, a type assertion or the end of the line.
125	WRAPPED = r'(?:[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(\s*)*(\w+)(?=\s*[,);!]|\s+as\b|\s+satisfies\b|\s*$)'

132	def exclusion(comp):
133	    """Why RDT's entry is not a component, from what RDT reports about it, or None. RDT lists every function it can
134	    give a parameter to, so hooks, route handlers, helpers and context objects come with it. The evidence is the shape:
135	    props that are the members of a TypeScript lib type (`String`, `Function`, `Request`) mean the parameter is not an
136	    object of props; a hook is named `use` and a capital; a `value` declared by `@types/react` and nothing else is a
137	    context's Provider; a lowercase name cannot be a JSX tag unless it takes the attributes of one (a `@types/react`
138	    prop) or is the file's or directory's own name, which RDT gives a default export; and props that are all promises
139	    are handed over by a router, not by a parent."""
140	    props = comp['props']
141	    in_lib = sum(bool(LIB_FILE.search(i.get('parent') or '')) for i in props.values())
142	    if in_lib * 2 > len(props):
143	        return 'lib_members'
144	    name = comp['name']
145	    if re.match(r'use[A-Z0-9]', name):
146	        return 'hook'
147	    if 'value' in props and set(props) <= {'value', 'children'} and all(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
148	        return 'context_value'
149	    if name[:1].islower() and norm_name(name) not in own_names(comp['file']) and not any(map(declared_in_react, props.values())):
150	        return 'not_jsx'
151	    if all(i.get('type', '').startswith('Promise<') for i in props.values()):
152	        return 'promise_props'
153	    return None

156	def read_text(path):
157	    """A source file's text, or None if there is no such file."""

164	def import_binding(text, name):
165	    """Where `name` was imported from in `text`: (module, imported name) or None."""
166	    for match in re.finditer(r"^import\s+(?:type\s+)?([^;'\"]*?)\s+from\s+['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text, re.M):
167	        clause, module = match.groups()
168	        if not clause.startswith('{'):
169	            default, _, clause = clause.partition(',')
170	            if default.strip() == name:
171	                return module, 'default'
172	        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', clause.partition('{')[2].partition('}')[0]):
173	            if (alias or original) == name:
174	                return module, original
175	    return None

178	def export_source(text, name):
179	    """How `text` exports `name` (`default` or a name): ('local', local name), ('from', module, name) or None."""
180	    if name == 'default':
181	        # The second pattern unwraps calls whose first argument is an identifier (`memo(Foo)`, `observer(forwardRef(Foo))`,
182	        # `Object.assign(Foo, {...})`), and a trailing assertion (`Foo as T`, `Foo satisfies T`, `Foo!`): the wrapper is
183	        # whatever function the file calls, so the name that matters is the innermost identifier.
184	        for pattern in (r'^export\s+default\s+(?:async\s+)?(?:function\*?|class)\s+(\w+)',
185	                        rf'^export\s+default\s+{WRAPPED}'):
186	            match = re.search(pattern, text, re.M)
187	            if match:
188	                return 'local', match.group(1)
189	    else:
190	        declaration = rf'^export\s+(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function\*?|class|async\s+function)\s+{re.escape(name)}\b'
191	        if re.search(declaration, text, re.M):
192	            return 'local', name
193	    for match in re.finditer(r"^export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*(?:from\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"])?", text, re.M):
194	        for original, alias in re.findall(r'(\w+)(?:\s+as\s+(\w+))?', match.group(1)):
195	            if (alias or original) == name:
196	                return ('from', match.group(2), original) if match.group(2) else ('local', original)
197	    return None

200	def resolve_module(file, module, exists):
201	    """The file `module` names from `file` (relative paths only), as a path relative to the root."""
202	    if not module.startswith('.'):
203	        return None
204	    base = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(file), module))
205	    return next((base + ext for ext in EXTENSIONS if exists(base + ext)), None)

208	def export_target(file, read, exists, name='default', hops=6):
209	    """The file and local name where what `file` exports as `name` is defined: follows `export default X`,
210	    `import X from`, `export { X } from` and `export { default as X }` through re-exports. None where it ends elsewhere."""
211	    text = read(file)
212	    exported = export_source(text, name) if text and hops else None
213	    if not exported:
214	        return None
215	    if exported[0] == 'from':
216	        target = resolve_module(file, exported[1], exists)
217	        return export_target(target, read, exists, exported[2], hops - 1) if target else None
218	    chain = local_chain(text, exported[1])
219	    for local in chain:
220	        imported = import_binding(text, local)
221	        if imported:
222	            target = resolve_module(file, imported[0], exists)
223	            return export_target(target, read, exists, imported[1], hops - 1) if target else None
224	    return file, exported[1]

227	def local_chain(text, name, hops=4):
228	    """`name` and what a chain of `const name = Other` / `const name = memo(Other)` in `text` leads to, nearest first:
229	    the component is declared under the last, and Caliper may report it under any of them."""
230	    names = [name]
231	    while text and len(names) <= hops:
232	        match = re.search(rf'^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+{re.escape(names[-1])}\b(?:\s*:[^=\n]+)?\s*=\s*{WRAPPED}',
233	                          text, re.M)
234	        if not match or match.group(1) in names:
235	            break
236	        names.append(match.group(1))
237	    return names

240	def display_assignments(text):
241	    """The `Foo.displayName = 'Bar'` assignments in `text`, as (local name, shown name) pairs."""
242	    return re.findall(r"^\s*(\w+)\.displayName\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text or '', re.M)

245	def own_names(file):
246	    """The names RDT gives a default export of `file`: the file's own, and its directory's."""
247	    return {norm_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(file))[0]), norm_name(os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(file)))}

250	def counterpart(file, name, found_by_file, read=None, claimed=()):
251	    """Caliper's key in `file` for a component called `name`, or None: the names must agree, since a file's only
252	    component says nothing about whether RDT's entry is that component. With `read`, the names a local alias chain
253	    leads to count too, and the `displayName` each is given; a key in `claimed` (one an RDT entry already matches
254	    exactly) is never the answer."""
255	    text = read(file) if read else None
256	    names = local_chain(text, name) if read else [name]
257	    # Caliper names a component by its `displayName` where there is one, RDT by the declaration.
258	    shown = dict(display_assignments(text))
259	    for candidate in [n for local in names for n in (local, shown.get(local)) if n]:
260	        key = (file, norm_name(candidate))
261	        if norm_name(candidate) in found_by_file.get(file, {}) and key not in claimed:
262	            return key
263	    return None

266	def pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists, claimed=()):
267	    """Caliper's key and the evidence for RDT's entry that Caliper does not report under its own key. In another file:
268	    where the default export of RDT's file is defined (RDT names a default export after the file or directory) or, for a
269	    named export, where that is. In the same file: the component that default export is, when the RDT name is the file's
270	    or directory's own and no other entry already matches it, or the one whose `displayName` RDT reports. Else the file
271	    that declares its props, when Caliper reports a component of that name there. A local alias chain
272	    (`const A = memo(B); export default A`) leads to the declaration. None if no evidence leads to a component."""
273	    file = relative(comp['file'], root)
274	    for export in ('default', comp['name']):
275	        target = export_target(file, read, exists, export)
276	        if not target:
277	            continue
278	        if target[0] != file:
279	            found = counterpart(target[0], target[1], found_by_file, read)
280	            if found:
281	                return found, 'default_export' if export == 'default' else 'named_export'
282	        elif export == 'default' and norm_name(comp['name']) in own_names(file):
283	            found = counterpart(file, target[1], found_by_file, read, claimed)
284	            if found:
285	                return found, 'default_alias'
286	    local = next((l for l, shown in display_assignments(read(file)) if norm_name(shown) == norm_name(comp['name'])), None)
287	    found = counterpart(file, local, found_by_file, read, claimed) if local else None
288	    if found:
289	        return found, 'display_name'
290	    name = norm_name(comp['name'])
291	    for info in comp['props'].values():
292	        parent = info.get('parent') or ''
293	        declared = relative(parent, root) if parent and REACT_DIR not in parent else None
294	        if declared and declared != file and name in found_by_file.get(declared, {}):
295	            return (declared, name), 'declaration'
296	    return None

302	def from_dependency(text, name):
303	    """Whether `text` imports `name` from a package (any form of import), not from a relative path."""
304	    for match in re.finditer(r"^import\s+(?:type\s+)?([^;'\"]*?)\s+from\s+['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", text, re.M):
305	        if not match.group(2).startswith('.') and re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(name)}\b', match.group(1)):
306	            return True
307	    return False

310	def reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, name, hops=6):
311	    """Whether what `file` exports as `name` ends in a package: `export { X } from 'pkg'`, or an import from one."""
312	    text = read(file)
313	    exported = export_source(text, name) if text and hops else None
314	    if not exported:
315	        return False
316	    if exported[0] == 'from':
317	        target = resolve_module(file, exported[1], exists)
318	        return reaches_dependency(target, read, exists, exported[2], hops - 1) if target else not exported[1].startswith('.')
319	    for local in local_chain(text, exported[1]):
320	        imported = import_binding(text, local)
321	        if imported:
322	            target = resolve_module(file, imported[0], exists)
323	            return reaches_dependency(target, read, exists, imported[1], hops - 1) if target else not imported[0].startswith('.')
324	    return False
325

327	def unmatched_cause(name, file, found_by_file, read, exists):
328	    """Why Caliper reports none of an item's names, from the item's file: a member of another component
329	    (`Form.List = List`); a member of an object literal (`logo: () => ...`); an alias of something a package exports
330	    (`const Tooltip = Recharts.Tooltip`); a value a call builds (`createIcon(...)`, `generateCalendar(...)`); a name the
331	    file exports from a package; else a component the file declares that Caliper does not report, in a file where it
332	    reports others or none. RDT names a default export after the file, so for that name the declaration is the one the
333	    default export leads to. The causes are what the file shows, so a cause says where to look, not what is wrong."""
334	    text = read(file) or ''
335	    names = [name.split('.')[-1]]
336	    default = norm_name(name) in own_names(file)
337	    exported = export_source(text, 'default') if default else None
338	    if exported and exported[0] == 'local':
339	        names += local_chain(text, exported[1])
340	    pattern = '(?:' + '|'.join(map(re.escape, dict.fromkeys(names))) + ')'
341	    declaration = rf'^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+{pattern}\b(?:\s*:[^=\n]+)?\s*=\s*'
342	    if re.search(rf'\b\w+\.{pattern}\s*=[^=]', text):
343	        return 'compound_member'
344	    if re.search(rf'^\s+{pattern}\s*:\s*(?:\(|<|function\b|async\b|[\w$]+\s*=>|(?:React\.)?(?:memo|forwardRef)\b)', text, re.M):
345	        return 'object_member'
346	    alias = re.search(declaration + r'(\w+)(?:\.\w+)*\s*;?\s*$', text, re.M)
347	    if alias and from_dependency(text, alias.group(1)):
348	        return 'dependency'
349	    if re.search(declaration + r'[\w.]+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\(', text, re.M):
350	        return 'call_result'
351	    if reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, name) or (default and reaches_dependency(file, read, exists, 'default')):
352	        return 'dependency'
353	    return 'file_with_other_components' if found_by_file.get(file) else 'file_without_components'

356	def reference(rdt_components, found, root):
357	    """The components recall is measured on, from RDT's output: entries with props, minus those that are not components
358	    (`exclusion`), with every RDT entry for one component counted once. An entry that Caliper reports under another file
359	    pairs with it by evidence (`pair`) and joins the entry in that file; RDT's repeats of one key join too. Each item is
360	    {'keys': every (file, name) a tool may report it under, 'props': prop -> 'own' | 'react'}, so one list serves every
361	    tool. Also the counts, so a change in the reference shows in weekly.json, and the items Caliper reports nowhere, by
362	    cause (`unmatched_cause`): a count per cause and the first `LIST_CAP` of each, as `file: name`."""
363	    found_by_file = {}
364	    for file, name in found:
365	        found_by_file.setdefault(file, {})[name] = None
366	    exists = lambda rel: os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, rel))
367	    read = lambda rel: read_text(os.path.join(root, rel))
368	    stats = {'rdt_with_props': 0, 'excluded': {}, 'exact': 0, 'paired': {}, 'merged': 0}
369	    entries = []
370	    for comp in rdt_components:
371	        if not comp['props']:
372	            continue
373	        stats['rdt_with_props'] += 1
374	        why = exclusion(comp)
375	        if why:
376	            stats['excluded'][why] = stats['excluded'].get(why, 0) + 1
377	            continue
378	        entries.append((comp, (relative(comp['file'], root), norm_name(comp['name']))))
379	    # Caliper's keys that an RDT entry matches exactly: another entry in that file is never paired with them.
380	    claimed = {key for _, key in entries if key in found}
381	    groups = {}
382	    for comp, key in entries:
383	        target = key if key in found else None
384	        if target:
385	            stats['exact'] += 1
386	        else:
387	            paired = pair(comp, root, found_by_file, read, exists, claimed)
388	            if paired:
389	                target = paired[0]
390	                stats['paired'][paired[1]] = stats['paired'].get(paired[1], 0) + 1
391	        keys = [key] + ([target] if target else [])
392	        group = groups.get(target or key)
393	        if group is None:
394	            group = groups[target or key] = {'keys': [], 'exact': {}, 'other': {}, 'file': key[0], 'name': comp['name']}
395	        else:
396	            stats['merged'] += 1
397	        group['keys'] += keys
398	        # The props of the entries in the component's own file when there are any, else of all the repeats united, so the
399	        # reference does not depend on the order RDT lists them in. A prop any repeat takes from `@types/react` is one.
400	        into = group['exact' if key == target else 'other']
401	        for prop, info in comp['props'].items():
402	            into[prop] = 'react' if into.get(prop) == 'react' or declared_in_react(info) else 'own'
403	    items = [{'keys': list(dict.fromkeys(g['keys'])), 'props': g['exact'] or g['other']} for g in groups.values()]
404	    stats['reference'] = len(items)
405	    missed = [g for g, item in zip(groups.values(), items) if not any(k in found for k in item['keys'])]
406	    stats['unpaired'] = len(missed)
407	    stats['unmatched'] = {'by_cause': {}, 'listed': {}}
408	    for g in sorted(missed, key=lambda g: (g['file'], g['name'])):
409	        cause = unmatched_cause(g['name'], g['file'], found_by_file, read, exists)
410	        stats['unmatched']['by_cause'][cause] = stats['unmatched']['by_cause'].get(cause, 0) + 1
411	        listed = stats['unmatched']['listed'].setdefault(cause, [])
412	        if len(listed) < LIST_CAP:
413	            listed.append(f"{g['file']}: {g['name']}")
414	    stats['excluded_total'] = sum(stats['excluded'].values())
415	    return items, stats

418	def recall(items, found, layered=None):
419	    """Against the reference: the components the tool also reports and, of those, RDT's props it lists, apart from and
420	    with `@types/react`'s, so a missing component and a missing prop are counted once each. `own` and `react` count the
421	    props listed as props; `own_layers` and `react_layers` also count those held in a collapsed layer (`layered`), which
422	    the output names without listing them."""
423	    layered = layered or {}
424	    count = {'components': [0, 0], 'own': [0, 0], 'react': [0, 0], 'own_layers': [0, 0], 'react_layers': [0, 0]}
425	    for item in items:
426	        count['components'][1] += 1
427	        key = next((k for k in item['keys'] if k in found), None)
428	        if key is None:
429	            continue
430	        in_layers = layered.get(key, set())
431	        count['components'][0] += 1
432	        for prop, kind in item['props'].items():
433	            count[kind][1] += 1
434	            count[kind][0] += prop in found[key]
435	            count[f'{kind}_layers'][1] += 1
436	            count[f'{kind}_layers'][0] += prop in found[key] or prop in in_layers
437	    return count

450	    """How often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types (apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts), and how RDT and
451	    react-docgen fare against it over the same props. `shared_props`, `agree` and `wrong` are Caliper's, over the props
452	    both list, and keep their meaning from week to week; `tools` holds all three over every prop the checker finds."""
453	    caliper_json = os.path.join(work, f'{name}.caliper.json')
454	    with open(caliper_json, 'w') as f:

456	                        '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none', '--quiet'], stdout=f, check=True)
457	    list_file, tsconfig = program_inputs(name, src, work)

529	    its recall against RDT by more than 2 points, which is not compared across references built by different rules, and the

552	def tool_line(corpus, tool, score):
553	    """One tool against the checker, in words: agreement of the whole universe first, then of what the tool lists, then
554	    what it omits by where the checker says the prop is declared."""
555	    s = score['missing_by_stratum']
556	    parts = [f"agrees on {100 * score['agree_universe']:.1f}% of the {score['universe']:,} props the checker finds "
557	             f"({100 * score['agree_listed']:.1f}% of the {score['listed']:,} it lists, "
558	             f"{100 * score['wrong_listed']:.2f}% of those wrong)",
559	             f"omits {sum(s.values()):,} ({s['same_file']:,} declared in the component's file, {s['other_project_file']:,} in "
560	             f"other project files, {s['dependency']:,} in dependencies, {s['unknown']:,} unknown)"]
561	    if score['missing_by_reason']['collapsed']:
562	        parts.append(f"{score['missing_by_reason']['collapsed']:,} more sit in collapsed layers")
563	    if score.get('failed_files'):

565	    return f"- {corpus}, {TOOL_LABELS[tool]}: " + '; '.join(parts)

1	// TypeScript 7.1's checker as a test oracle for Caliper's prop types (docs/parity.md). Test-only: the opt-in semantic
2	// backend is a separate, experimental feature.
3	//
4	// For one corpus, finds components the way react-docgen-typescript does (an exported function whose only or `props`
5	// parameter is the props type), reads each prop's type from the checker, and compares it structurally with the prop
6	// Caliper's canonical JSON reports for the same component (src/oracle-compare.ts). Each shared prop gets one verdict:
7	//
8	//   identical          both sides describe the same type
9	//   spelled            the same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it, or the reverse
10	//   less precise       Caliper's type is looser or unevaluated (an opaque type, `string` for a literal union, a name
11	//                      left unexpanded, a lost optional or rest parameter, a missing field)
12	//   wrong              Caliper's type describes something else
13	//   checker any/error  the checker itself has no type (an unresolved import, `any`, or `unknown` where Caliper has one)
14	//
15	// Checker types are normalized once per type id and verdicts made once per (Caliper prop, checker type), so Chakra's
16	// ~470,000 props cost a few thousand distinct comparisons.
17	//
18	// With `--rdt` and `--rdg` (the dumps scripts/rdt.mjs and scripts/rdg.mjs write) the report also scores react-docgen-
19	// typescript and react-docgen over every own prop the checker finds (`tools`; src/tool-universe.ts).

74	const rel = (path: string) => relative(root, realpathSync(path))

76	const caliper = assertSchemaVersion(JSON.parse(readFileSync(args.caliper, 'utf8')), 'caliper JSON')
77	checkCaliperShape(caliper)
78	const caliperByFile = new Map<string, { name: string; key: string; component: any }[]>()
79	for (const [componentKey, component] of Object.entries<any>(caliper.components)) {
80	  // Schema 2 lists a component's prop set ids, each a map of prop name to prop id; this reads one map of both.
81	  component.props = flattenProps(caliper, componentKey, component)
82	  const key = rel(component.filePath)
83	  const list = caliperByFile.get(key) ?? []
84	  list.push({ name: normComponent(component.displayName), key: componentKey, component })
85	  caliperByFile.set(key, list)
86	}
87	const rdt = loadTool(args.rdt, rel)
88	const rdg = loadTool(args.rdg, rel)
89	const universe = universeRecorder({ root, caliper, checker, checkerNorm, rdt, rdg })
90	
91	interface Example {
92	  component: string
93	  prop: string
94	  caliper: unknown
95	  checker: string
96	  normalized: object
97	}
98	const counts = Object.fromEntries(VERDICTS.map((v) => [v, 0])) as Record<Verdict, number>
99	const examples = Object.fromEntries(VERDICTS.map((v) => [v, [] as Example[]])) as Record<Verdict, Example[]>
100	const verdictCache = new Map<string, Verdict>()
101	const rows: [string, string, Verdict | 'missing' | 'collapsed'][] = []
102	const missingDetails: { key: string; prop: string; verdict: 'missing' | 'collapsed'; declarations: string[] }[] = []
103	const dumped: {
104	  key: string
105	  file: string
106	  component: string
107	  prop: string
108	  verdict: Verdict
109	  caliper: unknown
110	  checker: string
111	}[] = []
112	const totals = {
113	  componentsChecker: 0,
114	  componentsMatched: 0,
115	  propsChecker: 0,
116	  propsShared: 0,
117	  propsMissing: 0,
118	  propsCollapsed: 0,
119	  failedExports: 0,
120	  ambiguousExports: 0,
121	}
122	
123	/** The verdict for one prop, made once per (Caliper prop, checker type). */
124	function judge({
125	  component,
126	  prop,
127	  caliperId,
128	  type,
129	}: {
130	  component: string
131	  prop: string
132	  caliperId: string
133	  type: any
134	}) {
135	  const key = `${caliperId}:${type.id}`
136	  const cached = verdictCache.get(key)
137	  if (cached !== undefined) return cached
138	  const c: Norm = caliperNorm(caliper.props[caliperId].type)
139	  const k: Norm = checkerNorm(type)
140	  const verdict = compare(c, k)
141	  verdictCache.set(key, verdict)
142	  if (examples[verdict].length < 20) {
143	    const checkerText = checker.typeToString(type)
144	    examples[verdict].push({
145	      component,
146	      prop,
147	      caliper: caliper.props[caliperId].type,
148	      checker: checkerText,
149	      normalized: { caliper: c, checker: k },
150	    })
151	  }
152	  return verdict
153	}
154	
155	/** Every prop of one exported component the checker finds, against Caliper's component of the same name. */
156	function visitExport(exported: any, candidates: { name: string; key: string; component: any }[], file: string): void {
157	  let propsType
158	  try {
159	    propsType = propsTypeOf(checker, exported)
160	  } catch {
161	    totals.failedExports++
162	    return
163	  }
164	  if (!propsType) return
165	  const props = checker.getPropertiesOfType(propsType)
166	  if (props.length === 0) return
167	  totals.componentsChecker++
168	  const name = exportName(checker, exported)
169	  // React's DOM attributes are one inherited layer; ref and key are deliberately absent from Caliper's output.
170	  const own = props.filter(
171	    (p: any) =>
172	      p.name !== 'ref' &&
173	      p.name !== 'key' &&
174	      !p.declarations?.some((d: any) => String(d.path).includes('/@types/react/')),
175	  )
176	  totals.propsChecker += own.length
177	  const matches = candidates.filter((c) => c.name === normComponent(name))
178	  universe.record({ own, name, file, matches })
179	  if (matches.length > 1) {
180	    totals.ambiguousExports++
181	    return
182	  }
183	  const [match] = matches
184	  if (!match) return
185	  totals.componentsMatched++
186	  const shared = own.filter((p: any) => Object.hasOwn(match.component.props, p.name))
187	  const layerFiles = collapsedLayerFiles(caliper, match.component)
188	  const absent = own.filter((p: any) => !Object.hasOwn(match.component.props, p.name))
189	  const collapsed: any[] = []
190	  const missing: any[] = []
191	  for (const p of absent) {
192	    if (p.declarations?.some((d: any) => layerFiles.has(pathKey(String(d.path))))) collapsed.push(p)
193	    else missing.push(p)
194	  }
195	  totals.propsMissing += missing.length
196	  totals.propsCollapsed += collapsed.length
197	  if (args.rows) rows.push(...missing.map((p: any) => [match.key, p.name, 'missing'] as [string, string, 'missing']))
198	  if (args.rows)
199	    rows.push(...collapsed.map((p: any) => [match.key, p.name, 'collapsed'] as [string, string, 'collapsed']))
200	  if (args.missing) {
201	    for (const [verdict, absentProps] of [
202	      ['missing', missing],
203	      ['collapsed', collapsed],
204	    ] as const) {
205	      for (const p of absentProps) {
206	        missingDetails.push({
207	          key: match.key,
208	          prop: p.name,
209	          verdict,
210	          declarations: p.declarations?.map((d: any) => String(d.path)) ?? [],
211	        })
212	      }
213	    }
214	  }
215	  if (shared.length === 0) return
216	  const types = checker.getTypeOfSymbol(shared)
217	  for (const [i, p] of shared.entries()) {
218	    totals.propsShared++
219	    const caliperId = match.component.props[p.name]
220	    const verdict = judge({ component: name, prop: p.name, caliperId, type: types[i] })
221	    counts[verdict]++
222	    if (args.rows) rows.push([match.key, p.name, verdict])
223	    if (args.dump && (verdict === 'wrong' || verdict === 'less precise')) {
224	      dumped.push({
225	        key: match.key,
226	        file: rel(file),
227	        component: name,
228	        prop: p.name,
229	        verdict,
230	        caliper: caliper.props[caliperId].type,
231	        checker: checker.typeToString(types[i]),
232	      })
233	    }
234	  }
235	}
236	
237	const start = performance.now()
238	for (const file of files) {
239	  const moduleSymbol = checker.getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)
240	  if (!moduleSymbol) continue
241	  const candidates = caliperByFile.get(rel(file)) ?? []
242	  for (const exported of checker.getExportsOfModule(moduleSymbol)) visitExport(exported, candidates, file)
243	}
244	const compareMs = performance.now() - start
245	requireComparison(totals.propsShared, totals.componentsMatched)
246	
247	const report = {
248	  components_checker: totals.componentsChecker,
249	  components_matched: totals.componentsMatched,
250	  props_checker: totals.propsChecker,
251	  props_shared: totals.propsShared,
252	  props_missing: totals.propsMissing,
253	  props_collapsed: totals.propsCollapsed,
254	  verdicts: counts,
255	  distinct_comparisons: verdictCache.size,
256	  failed_exports: totals.failedExports,
257	  ambiguous_exports: totals.ambiguousExports,
258	  program_ms: Math.round(programMs),
259	  compare_ms: Math.round(compareMs),
260	  tools: universe.score(counts),
261	  examples,
262	}
263	writeFileSync(args.out, JSON.stringify(report, null, 2))
264	if (args.dump) writeFileSync(args.dump, JSON.stringify(dumped))
265	if (args.rows) writeFileSync(args.rows, JSON.stringify(rows))
266	if (args.missing) writeFileSync(args.missing, JSON.stringify(missingDetails))
267	program.dispose()
268	api.close()
269	console.error(
270	  `${totals.componentsMatched}/${totals.componentsChecker} components, ${totals.propsShared} shared props, ` +
271	    `${verdictCache.size} distinct comparisons, program ${(programMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s, ` +
272	    `compare ${(compareMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`,
273	)

1	// Scores one tool (Caliper, react-docgen-typescript or react-docgen) against the checker over the same universe of props,
2	// so the three are held to the same rules. Pure: nothing here talks to the checker or reads a file.
3	//
4	// The universe is every own prop the checker finds on a component export (React's inherited DOM attributes, `ref` and
5	// `key` are not part of it; src/oracle.ts filters them). A tool's prop is `listed` when the tool reports it, and gets
6	// the same verdict the oracle gives Caliper (src/oracle-compare.ts); otherwise it is `missing`, for one of three
7	// reasons, and counted by where the checker says the prop is declared.
8	import { compare, VERDICTS, type Norm, type Verdict } from './oracle-compare.ts'
9	
10	/** Where a prop the tool does not list is declared, by the checker's first declaration. */
11	export const STRATA = ['same_file', 'other_project_file', 'dependency', 'unknown'] as const
12	export type Stratum = (typeof STRATA)[number]
13	
14	/** Why a tool does not list a prop: it reports no such component, the tool threw on the component's file, it reports
15	 * the component but not that prop, or it lists the prop only as a member of an inherited layer it collapsed
16	 * (Caliper's `inheritance`, which is a deliberate choice, not an omission). */
17	export const REASONS = ['component', 'failed_file', 'prop', 'collapsed'] as const
18	export type Reason = (typeof REASONS)[number]
19	
20	/** One prop the checker finds, with the checker's type already reduced to a `Norm`. */
21	export interface UniverseProp {
22	  /** The component, as the tools are matched to it: file and normalised name. */
23	  component: string
24	  prop: string
25	  stratum: Stratum
26	  checker: Norm
27	}
28	
29	/** What a tool reports for a universe prop: its type as a `Norm`, or why it has none. */
30	export type Reported = Norm | Reason
31	
32	export interface ToolScore {
33	  /** Props the checker finds on the components of the universe. */
34	  universe: number
35	  listed: number
36	  missing: number
37	  verdicts: Record<Verdict, number>
38	  /** Identical or spelled, of the whole universe: a prop the tool omits counts against it. */
39	  agree_universe: number
40	  /** Identical or spelled, of the props the tool lists. */
41	  agree_listed: number
42	  /** Wrong, of the props the tool lists. */
43	  wrong_listed: number
44	  missing_by_stratum: Record<Stratum, number>
45	  missing_by_reason: Record<Reason, number>
46	  /** Components with at least one prop in the universe, and how many of them the tool reports at all. */
47	  components: number
48	  components_found: number
49	  /** The first few props of each kind the tool gets wrong or less precise, to review the adapters by. */
50	  examples: Record<'wrong' | 'less precise', { component: string; prop: string; tool: Norm; checker: Norm }[]>
51	}
52	
53	const EXAMPLES = 8
54	
55	const isReason = (value: Reported): value is Reason => typeof value === 'string'
56	const rate = (n: number, of: number) => (of === 0 ? 0 : n / of)
57	
58	/** `pick` says what the tool reports for one universe prop. */
59	export function scoreTool<T extends UniverseProp>(universe: readonly T[], pick: (u: T) => Reported): ToolScore {
60	  const verdicts = Object.fromEntries(VERDICTS.map((v) => [v, 0])) as Record<Verdict, number>
61	  const byStratum = Object.fromEntries(STRATA.map((s) => [s, 0])) as Record<Stratum, number>
62	  const byReason = Object.fromEntries(REASONS.map((r) => [r, 0])) as Record<Reason, number>
63	  const components = new Set<string>()
64	  const found = new Set<string>()
65	  const examples: ToolScore['examples'] = { wrong: [], 'less precise': [] }
66	  let listed = 0
67	  for (const u of universe) {
68	    components.add(u.component)
69	    const reported = pick(u)
70	    // A component is found when any of its props is not missing for want of the component itself.
71	    if (!isReason(reported) || (reported !== 'component' && reported !== 'failed_file')) found.add(u.component)
72	    if (isReason(reported)) {
73	      byReason[reported]++
74	      // A collapsed layer is a choice, not an omission, so it has no stratum.
75	      if (reported !== 'collapsed') byStratum[u.stratum]++
76	      continue
77	    }
78	    listed++
79	    const verdict = compare(reported, u.checker)
80	    verdicts[verdict]++
81	    if ((verdict === 'wrong' || verdict === 'less precise') && examples[verdict].length < EXAMPLES) {
82	      examples[verdict].push({
83	        component: u.component.replace('\0', ' '),
84	        prop: u.prop,
85	        tool: reported,
86	        checker: u.checker,
87	      })
88	    }
89	  }
90	  const agree = verdicts.identical + verdicts.spelled
91	  return {
92	    universe: universe.length,
93	    listed,
94	    missing: universe.length - listed,
95	    verdicts,
96	    agree_universe: rate(agree, universe.length),
97	    agree_listed: rate(agree, listed),
98	    wrong_listed: rate(verdicts.wrong, listed),
99	    missing_by_stratum: byStratum,
100	    missing_by_reason: byReason,
101	    components: components.size,
102	    components_found: found.size,
103	    examples,
104	  }
105	}
106	
107	/** Like `scoreTool`, over the components the tool reports only: a prop of a component the tool does not report at all
108	 * (`component`) is left out, so a function the checker takes for a component and the tool rightly ignores does not
109	 * count against it. This is the universe of the weekly headline: what a reader of the tool's output is shown. */
110	export function scoreReported<T extends UniverseProp>(universe: readonly T[], pick: (u: T) => Reported): ToolScore {
111	  return scoreTool(
112	    universe.filter((u) => pick(u) !== 'component'),
113	    pick,
114	  )
115	}
